definitions.explanation: Something that breaks from the norm or standard, especially in a positive or remarkable way.
A price far below the expected or usual amount.

examples.japanese: {破格|はかく}の{待遇|たいぐう}を{受|う}けた。
{若|わか}くして{社長|しゃちょう}に{抜擢|ばってき}されるのは{破格|はかく}のことだ。
examples.english: Being promoted to company president at a young age is an extraordinary thing.

examples.japanese: あの{選手|せんしゅ}は{破格|はかく}の{才能|さいのう}の{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}で、{入団|にゅうだん}{一年目|いちねんめ}から{活躍|かつやく}している。
examples.english: That athlete has extraordinary talent and has been excelling since their first year.

examples.japanese: {破格|はかく}の{値段|ねだん}で{買|か}えた。
examples.english: I was able to buy it at a bargain price.

examples.japanese: このレストランは{破格|はかく}の{安|やす}さで{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: This restaurant is popular for its exceptionally low prices.

examples.japanese: {閉店|へいてん}セールで{高級|こうきゅう}ブランドの{服|ふく}が{破格|はかく}の{値段|ねだん}で{売|う}られていたので、まとめ{買|が}いした。
examples.english: Luxury brand clothing was being sold at bargain prices in the closing sale, so I bought in bulk.

notes:
Literally "breaking the standard" — composed of {破|は} (break) + {格|かく} (standard, rank). Used as a の-adjective to modify nouns. The word carries a positive nuance, emphasizing that something exceeds expectations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {破格|はかく}の{値段|ねだん}: bargain price
- {破格|はかく}の{待遇|たいぐう}: exceptional treatment
- {破格|はかく}の{安|やす}さ: exceptional cheapness
- {破格|はかく}の{条件|じょうけん}: extraordinary terms/conditions
- {破格|はかく}の{才能|さいのう}: exceptional talent

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {格安|かくやす}: discount, cheap — specifically about low prices, less emphatic
- {異例|いれい}: exceptional, unprecedented — focuses on being unusual, not necessarily positive
- {特別|とくべつ}: special — more general and neutral
